title: Oncall choreography and pager signal calibrator for multi-region degradation
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Reduce noisy pages during region-level degradations while ensuring rapid, context-rich escalation when customer-impacting SLOs cross thresholds. Deliver an automated 'signal calibrator' service + oncall choreography templates that gate and enrich alerts for multi-region failover and load-shedding events.

Background: Over the last two quarters we observed many small regional incidents escalate to pages due to threshold sensitivity and duplicated signals across related services (serving runtime, routing, cache eviction). This causes oncall fatigue and slows response to genuine degradations. We need a middleware that applies SLO-aware filtering, deduplication, and progressive severity promotion tied to circuit-breaker state and active failover progress.

Acceptance criteria:
- New signal calibrator service deployed behind feature flag in prod that consumes alert stream and emits enriched incidents or suppressed signals.
- Pager volume from region-degraded incidents reduced by >= 60% in pilot region without increasing mean time to mitigation (MTTM) for high-severity incidents.
- Oncall choreography templates (step-by-step run instructions) published in Confluence and linked from enriched incidents.
- Automated escalation integration with our incident orchestrator for graduated promotion (silent -> slack -> page) and automatic rollback of suppression if a regression is detected.
- Unit & integration tests + canary in us-west-2 operating for two weeks with metrics dashboard.

Proposed approach:
1) Define SLO-derived signal tiers: observation, degraded, critical. Map thresholds across token latency p95, error-rate-5m, KV-miss-rate.
2) Build a lightweight calibrator that ingests alerts (Alertmanager webhook), attaches context (active failover plan, circuit-breaker state, recent traffic shifts), and runs policy rules: dedupe by correlation keys, suppress transient flaps under hysteresis, group signals by impacted surface, and escalate after time-based windows.
3) Implement 'circuit breaker gate' that automatically increases suppression aggressiveness when a region is already in partial evacuation and ramps it down as capacity stabilizes.
4) Create oncall choreography templates: a single-page 'triage checklist', 'gradual cutover checklist', 'controlled load-shed checklist', and 'post-incident verification checklist' tailored to multi-region semantics.
5) Alert enrichment: include timeline of key events, links to current routing/fallback policy, last 12 KV cache hit ratios, and recent rollout IDs.
6) Automate escalation flows via incident orchestrator with tags to allow immediate page for customer-impacting anomalies.

Rollout plan:
- Week 1: implement calibrator prototype + unit tests.
- Week 2: integration tests with Alertmanager + incident orchestrator in staging.
- Week 3: canary in us-west-2 with suppressed paging to oncall, collect metrics.
- Week 4: enable graduated paging for pilot team and update runbooks.
- Week 5-6: evaluate results and iterate before wider region rollout.

Metrics to monitor:
- Pager volume for region degradations (baseline vs pilot).
- Mean time to mitigation (MTTM) for critical incidents.
- False suppression rate (incidents suppressed that should have paged).
- Time-to-escalation when progressive promotion is used.

Notes on trade-offs: aggressive suppression reduces noise but risks missed early signals. To mitigate, we will prefer progressive promotion windows and require at least one high-confidence signal (e.g., sustained p95 latency > X and error-rate > Y) to fast-track paging.

comments: 2026-02-20 — Spike: validated correlation keys for dedupe using trace_id + route + model_version across 48h of historical alerts. Observed 72% duplication across services for the same underlying cause.
2026-02-24 — Design review with SRE and PMs: agreed on three-tier signal model and hysteresis windows (observation=1m, degraded=5m, critical=1m but need 2 signals). Liam to prototype policy DSL.
2026-02-28 — PR opened: github.com/redwood-inference/calibrator/pull/142 (prototype ingest + dedupe logic). Requesting eng-arch review from Priya. Linked unit tests and sample alert fixtures.
2026-03-02 — Canary config drafted: feature flag calibrator.us-west-2=true; escalation mapping added to incident-orchestrator. Ops runbook draft uploaded to Confluence.

2026-03-04 — Integration smoke: calibrator consumed staging alert stream and correctly grouped 9/10 related alerts into single enriched incident. One case of over-suppression found and rule tightened.
2026-03-05 — Security note: no elevated privileges required; uses read-only copies of routing state. Security review requested next cycle.
